findings.title: Calendar outage escapes as an unmapped traceback instead of exit 4
findings.description: `calendar_sessions` catches only `psycopg.OperationalError` and `CalendarNotFoundError` around `sessions_between`. `TradingCalendar` reads through `self._pool.connection()` (`src/manta_trading/data/base/trading_calendar.py:194`). An unreachable server through `psycopg_pool` surfaces as `PoolTimeout`, not `OperationalError`. The codebase already catches it for this reason (`src/manta_trading/cli/commands/data.py:416`, `src/manta_trading/data/acquisition/daemon/daily.py:770`). `PoolTimeout` is not in `exit_code_for` (`src/manta_trading/cli/commands/tick_exit.py:54-57`), so `run_mapped` re-raises it and the user gets a traceback. That contradicts the module docstring ("a calendar … outage raises (→ exit 4)") and `READ_EPILOG`. The only unreachable-database test covers the tick database (`test/integration/data/test_tick_status_cli.py`, `test_an_unreachable_tick_database_exits_4`). Separately, `OutOfPopulatedRangeError` also maps to exit 4 through `TickCalendarError`, which the epilog's "unreachable" wording does not describe. I could not reproduce the pool behavior here. The basis is the library's documented behavior plus the codebase's own handlers. Fix: catch `PoolTimeout` alongside `OperationalError`, and add a test with a closed calendar port.

findings.title: `caught_up` reports a result when the wanted range is unknown
findings.description: `wanted` becomes `None` when `_wanted_end` returns `None`, which happens when a tier is set, the universe `end` is unset, and no edge row exists. `_scope` then ignores the wanted range. Line 217 still passes `wanted=wanted_start is not None`, so `caught_up` is evaluated over held sessions alone and can return `True`. The output then reads "caught up: yes" next to "edge: never observed". `caught_up`'s own contract says `None` means no wanted range (`src/manta_trading/data/tick/tick_status.py:152-156`). Fix: `wanted=wanted is not None`. This is latent today because the only universe entry has `tier=None` (`src/manta_trading/data/tick/universe.py:45-47`).

findings.title: The raw-count proof is not scoped to the product
findings.description: `raw_counts` counts every `tick_trade` row in each session window, with no filter on instrument or unit. `_session_row` (`src/manta_trading/data/tick/tick_coverage.py:81-90`) builds its instrument list from every key in `raw`, so any instrument with raw rows but no ledger row for this shape is reported as a mismatch, and the verb exits 3. `tick_trade` is one table for all products. It has no product column (`src/manta_trading/market/schema/migrations/tick.py:222-245`), and the universe comment says slice 231 adds GC. Once a second product is ingested, `mt data tick coverage --product ES` will flag that product's instruments. This is not reachable today because only ES is configured, and the single-product tests cannot show it. `tick_trade.unit_id` is `NOT NULL` (`tick.py:244`), so scoping the scan to the shape's current unit ids would also give an exact per-unit match against the ledger. Add a test that inserts a row for another instrument inside a session window and asserts `check == "ok"`.

findings.title: `age()` prints nonsense for negative ages
findings.description: `edge_age_seconds` is `now - observed_at` (`tick_status_build.py:212`). `now` comes from the status host's clock, and `observed_at` is the `now` the acquiring run passed to `_upsert_edge` (`src/manta_trading/data/tick/availability.py:108-118`), not a database default. Any skew of one second or more makes the age negative. `age` does not guard for that, and `divmod` floors the negative values, so `age(-30)` returns `"-1d 23h"`. The line then prints "observed -1d 23h ago". Fix: handle negative ages explicitly (for example, "clock skew: observed N s in the future"). Add a unit test for negative and zero input. No test covers `age` today.

findings.title: `build_coverage` has no range guard
findings.description: The `end <= start` check exists only in the CLI (`src/manta_trading/cli/commands/tick_store_cmds.py:216-222`). `build_coverage` is the function slice 230's API is meant to serialize (per the `tick_status_build` docstring). With `end <= start`, the session filter `start <= s.session_date < end` matches nothing, so the result has `mismatched: false` and reads as a pass. Fix: validate in `build_coverage` and raise, and keep the CLI's friendly message.

findings.title: The raw-count scan has no supporting index, and its plan is unverified
findings.description: The `tick_trade` key is `(instrument_id, ts_event, sequence, sequence_ordinal)`, and the migration says "no index beyond the key" (`tick.py:215-218`). `raw_counts` joins with a non-equality `ts_event BETWEEN open AND close` against an unnest of sessions. Nothing in the schema supports a `ts_event` range scan, so each session window may read whole chunks. The docstring's "the one scan" is therefore unverified. `sql.md` asks for `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` before performance claims. I could not run it here. Run it on a realistic multi-month range and record the result before relying on coverage over long ranges.

findings.title: Tier-configured status logic has no integration coverage
findings.description: Every integration test uses the ES entry, which has `tier=None` (`universe.py:45-47`). Untested end to end: `_wanted_end` and the wanted-range scope in `_scope`; the `caught up: yes/no; holed [...]` rendering (`tick_status_render.py:84-87`); the `tier: …, wanted from` line; and holed-session reporting in a wanted range. `test_tick_status.py` covers `caught_up` in isolation only. Caught-up and holed sessions are the verb's main reporting, so add an integration test that sets a tier and an edge and asserts that output. Such a test would also catch the `caught_up` bug above.

findings.title: `_product_lines` is 54 lines and builds five sections
findings.description: This is over the ~50-line guideline. Splitting it into `_edge_lines`, `_bucket_lines`, and `_contract_lines` would make each piece small and testable. `lines[-1] += …` also mutates the last bucket row by index, which is easy to misread.

findings.title: Current units are loaded twice per product
findings.description: `_scope` calls `shape_units`, and `session_verdicts` calls it again for the same shape (line 87). Both are full scans of the shape's current units across all dates, once per product per invocation. Pass one result into both. This is minor at current volume, and I did not measure it.

findings.title: Connections and row types are loosened to `Any` or `str`
findings.description: `_read` and the coverage `read` take `Any` for the connection, though `Conn` is already defined in `manifest_reads.py` and used across the data layer. `raw_counts` takes `Sequence[tuple[date, int, int]]`, which a named type would make clearer. `CoverageSession.status` and `condition` are `str`, though `TickSessionStatus` exists. Use `Conn` and the enum types.

findings.title: Helpers used across modules live in the wrong place
findings.description: `tick_coverage` imports `calendar_sessions`, `jsonable`, `session_verdicts`, and `shape_of` from `tick_status_build`, so coverage depends on the status builder. `jsonable` is generic serialization and belongs in a shared utility module. Moving `calendar_sessions` and `jsonable` out would leave `tick_coverage` depending only on shared code.

findings.title: The `setup_logging` patch and its rationale are copied into three new test files
findings.description: `_app_patches`, the `no_key` fixture in `test_tick_ingest_cli.py`, and the autouse `settings` fixture in `test_data_tick_ingest.py` each repeat the same patch with the same comment. The wider suite already repeats it in about 40 files, so this predates the slice. The slice still adds three more copies, and the project rules ask for shared logic to live in one place. Consider one shared fixture in `test/conftest.py`.

findings.title: Test DELETEs only target a database the fixture created
findings.description: `migrated_tick_db` comes from `ephemeral_tick_db`, which uses `_throwaway_database` (`test/conftest.py:301-309`, `:194-226`). That helper creates the database and drops it on exit. The `DELETE FROM tick_trade` in this file and in `test_tick_status_cli.py` target that throwaway database, and neither file reads the production URL variable.

findings.title: The session-days refactor and the import trim preserve behavior
findings.description: `days_touched` keeps the original loop's semantics, and the caller applies the same `start <= day < end` filter. `ingest_plan.py` now uses the public `utc_midnight`, and its trimmed `datetime`/`UTC`/`time` imports have no remaining uses. No `_midnight` or `_utc_midnight` references remain in the repo.

findings.title: The writers still exit 1 on an unreachable tick database
findings.description: `TickDatabaseUnreachable` subclasses `TickPreflightError`, so `exit_code_for` still maps it to exit 1 for the writers. The read verbs check the subclass first in `run_mapped` (`tick_store_cmds.py:78`) and exit 4. `test_an_unreachable_tick_database_exits_4` covers this.

findings.title: Status and coverage SQL binds every value
findings.description: Every value goes through `%s` placeholders or the `shape.params()` dict. The interpolated fragments (`_UNITS`, `_LEDGER_UNITS`, `_SHAPE_WHERE`, `COVERAGE_PREDICATE`) are module constants with no user input. This follows the `LiteralString` pattern already used in `manifest_reads.py`.
